newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds recede, await payrolls data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds recede, await payrolls data.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities stumbled with Treasuries through much of a quiet session as market participants geared up for Friday's payrolls data, mortgage experts said.
Yield spreads narrowed slightly to Treasuries, but traders said the market is very jittery in anticipation of the February jobs data.

"I've been looking for stuff to buy and just haven't been able to," said one trader at a Midwest bank. "With the (employment) number looming tomorrow, I don't think there is much attractiveness," he said.
Overall, pass-through prices were 2/32 to 9/32 lower.

In late trading, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent paper had fallen 7/32 at 99-17/32, yielding 101 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note. Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were 7/32 lower as well, at 99-16/32 and 99-22/32, respectively. The 10-year Treasury note was off 10/32 at 97-12/32 to yield 6.61 percent.

The Labor Department is set to release the employment report at 0830 EST/1330 GMT. Economists polled by Reuters expected payrolls would show a gain of 230,000 and the unemployment rate would dip to 5.3 percent.
Looking forward, one trader said the recent decline in prices is healthy.
"This will give you a decent chance to invest," he said.
At this point, however, it is not advisable to hold premium paper, he said. "Unless they're seasoned, you would want to go down in coupon or even just buy Treasuries."
